text:
Andrew: FYI PR #3124 is blocked by CI — repeatedly failing a snapshot on mac shard-2 (embed-index-test). Not seeing any code changes that would cause this. Anyone seen this nondeterministic snapshot pattern before?

Maria: Can you paste the failing assertion + a small log snippet?

Andrew: Sure — here's the top of the failure:```
FAIL test/embed_index_test.go:42: expected 128 embeddings, got 127
--- /workspace/snapshots/embed-index/mac-shard-2/snap1.txt
+ actual /tmp/build/build-3124/output/snap1.txt
panic: index out of range
```

Jing: That 127 vs 128 smell like a map iteration order leak or a race in the test setup. We've hit similar before when tests relied on Go map order for deterministic snapshot outputs. Does the test iterate over a map without sorting?

Andrew: I checked — it uses a map to build the index keys then writes them out. We didn't touch that file in this PR.

Sam: Can we do a targeted rerun on mac shard-2 (only) to see if it's a transient flake? I can kick that off. /rerun pr=3124 shard=mac-2

SRE Bot: Targeted rerun started for PR 3124 (shard mac-2). Queue pos: 3.

Eli: Heads-up — I triggered a local run and saw the same failure once, but a second run passed. So it's flaky. If it's nondet map ordering, a minimal fix is to sort keys before writing snapshot.

Maria: If we confirm it's nondet, we should either: 1) fix the test to sort deterministic output, or 2) pin the snapshot update with a clear test change. We should avoid blindly updating snapshots.

Andrew: Agreed. I can add stable sort to the test within this PR. Question: would that require a snapshot update? Ideally not — sorting should make the output match the existing golden.

Jing: If current snapshot assumes a particular order that is unstable, sorting will stabilize and should match the golden unless the golden was produced with a different sort. But usually sorting to a canonical order avoids future flakes.

Sam: Rerun finished: all checks passed on mac-2 this time. But that's only one pass. Recommend merging only after we land the deterministic change.

Andrew: I'll push a tiny change to test to sort keys and push. Pinging reviewers @Maria @Jing — can you take a quick look when CI finishes? :pray:

Maria: Can do. If CI still flakes after sorting, we'll request a broader rerun and consider bisecting to isolate a flake.

Eli: Also consider adding a short retry in the test harness around index build — if the underlying index builder has nondet timing, that helps. But prefer deterministic ordering first.

Andrew: Pushed: added sort(keys) in embed_index_test.go and an extra assert to confirm len==128 before snapshot write. Triggered CI.

SRE Bot: Full CI started for PR 3124.

Sam: If CI passes once, I'll do one targeted rerun to be safe and then approve merge if green. :thumbsup:

Maria: Quick note — if you end up updating the snapshot intentionally, run `make test -update` and add a short changelog line in the PR describing why. Reviewers will expect that.

Andrew: Understood. Will report back after CI results. Thanks all.

Eli: One last thing — if CI shows different failures across mac shards, open an incidents/flake ticket so SRE can correlate infra variance.

Andrew: Will do if it recurs. Last update: mac shards passed, windows and linux green. Marking as ready-for-review and pinging reviewers again.

Maria: Reviewing now. If no regressions, let's merge after a final quick rerun by Sam.

Sam: Doing final targeted rerun now.

SRE Bot: Targeted rerun completed for PR 3124 — all green.

Maria: Approved. :white_check_mark:

Andrew: Thanks everyone — merging shortly.
